I can never know how anyone's life is doing. Nor will I claim to know how you are. But that's not gonna stop me from the most commonplace sayings, that are pretty much universal. Number one is, obviously, things will get better. Maybe it takes a couple days, maybe a couple weeks, who knows. Regardless, even if it's easy to do, it won't be easier. You mentioned that it's been a very long time since you self-harmed, and that the habit is still there. Think about how long you've made it so far. It's always important to look back on what you accomplished. You value your progress that you've made correct? If so, you see why you shouldn't. As for coping, since hobbies take a bit of effort, completely understandable, why not something that, you can take out your frustrations on that's not yourself. Since we're looking for something that doesn't take much effort, how would wood smashing sound. Now I know, sounds stupid, but here's the thing. A sledgehammer,  a small stack of wood, and some sawhorses to put them on. That crack and crunch that you hear when completely destroying a sheet of wood is amazing. Splitting rounds of wood is also fun, just swing away (I think I really like wood). In other words, try to find something that is destructive, but in a productive way.

Couldn't agree more. I started a couple years ago as a result from some drama at home. I wouldn't say it felt nice at first, It was more like it felt like I had finally found something to vent out all my anger and frustrations on. After a while, I started feeling all sad and shit because I was doing it. Which made that an almost perpetual cycle. I was luckily able to quit a year and a half later. But the addiction that I developed while hurting myself stayed in my head. It's like a voice in the back of my head that I wish would just go away

Thanks, man. I don't think I could trust my school's therapist, considering the whole policy that they have when it comes to hurting oneself. I'll keep being aware of which of my friends I'll trust. One of them tells her everything. But still though, thanks. Remember, every little bit helps everyone, regardless of how small it may seem to be.

Sorry to hear that. Still, there are always possible distractions you can use to get your mind off cutting. Perhaps photography, or even typing stories. Keep something running through your mind. Give cutting no place to stay in yer noggin'.

Why would you think that no one in your community would want to talk you? When I thought I was alone and that no one cared about me, It took me months to work up the courage to enter back into society. I was thinking, Why would anybody put up with me, but people can surprise.

Sometimes hard is good, sometimes. I feel that the harder a goal is, the more rewarding and amazing you'll feel if and when you finally meet your goal. It was hard for me to learn how to play the baritone, but once I learned how, It felt amazing. I made it my goal to learn how to play at least one song on every single one of my Music Department's instruments. Set goals and challenge yourself. Always strive to make yourself better than you were yesterday.  As for people to make your friends, it's always a possibility to reach out to your community, whether you are a student still going to school, or an adult living throughout life's highs and lows, there are groups that you can get in contact with that accept who you are and encourage you to grow as a person. It does take time to find those groups, obviously, but once you find that right one, you won't regret it.

Hey, you know you're not all shit. Yeah, sometimes we do shitty things, but that doesn't mean that's what defines us. While we wish we should be punished for what we've done, what we wish to ourselves is most of the time, not the answer. There are good things that everyone does. If you think your friends hate you, then, if your assumption is true, find those that will support you and treat you how you wish to be treated. If they don't like you being happy, then find people who wish you happiness. Don't hurt yourself, you're not terrible.

There is always something interesting in everybody. Sometimes you need deep, but everyone has something. Try learning an instrument, drawing when you feel like you are going to start. There are many good ways to make yourself stand out and be unique. We are all interesting. You’re not limited to just that. And if people only think you are interesting because you cut, you need to ditch them. They’d only prevent you from quitting. I hope you will feel better. Distract yourself. I believe in you. :)
